description: Hourglass-shaped two-portal arena. A narrow neck constricts the floor between two wider lobes (north and south). The straight-line path runs north-south through the neck. Detour anchors around the edges of each lobe let the autopilot investigate corner objectives without losing the neck route.

portals.north: spawn_north at (0.03, -23.47) — gate at the north (low-Z) end of the north lobe
portals.south: spawn_south at (-0.15, 23.44) — gate at the south (high-Z) end of the south lobe

anchors.description: south lobe staging (matches x2ua) — branches to south-lobe edges + into the neck
north end of the neck transition (matches xq2i)
south end of the neck transition (matches 6ucp)
north lobe staging (matches nshe) — branches to north-lobe edges + back through the neck
east corner of south lobe (matches g8leij)
west corner of north lobe (matches s04c21)

traversalNotes: Direct N↔S route: spawn_south → south_lobe_mid → neck_north → neck_south → north_lobe_mid → spawn_north (and reverse). Five hops, all axis-aligned-ish through the neck.

DISPATCH RULE: any objective in a corner of either lobe routes through the lobe's mid-staging anchor (south_lobe_mid or north_lobe_mid) — not directly from the spawn. e.g. south_lobe_west requires south_lobe_mid → south_lobe_west → south_lobe_mid → next leg.

The narrow NECK between neck_north and neck_south is the only connection between the lobes — the solver must NOT emit cross-lobe edges that bypass the neck, even if mesh validation passes (the visible width might be a sloped wall the autopilot would slip on).

Hourglass topology generalizes: any two-portal room with a constriction can use this anchor pattern (gate ↔ lobe_mid ↔ neck_lobe ↔ neck_other ↔ lobe_mid ↔ gate, plus lobe_mid → corner-detour branches).
